description: Builds and maintains the ransomware, payment portal and data-leak site; recruits affiliates. The 'platform' in the affiliate model.
revenue_share_or_price: Developer keeps ~15-30% of each ransom; LockBit admin took 20%
evidence: DOJ: LockBit administrator 'typically received a 20% share of each ransom payment'; group attacked 2,500+ victims in 120+ countries and extracted at least $500m; admin's personal share at least $100m
source_title: US Charges Russian National Developing/Operating LockBit
notes: Conti (2021-22 leaks) ran ~62 core staff (peak ~100), programmers salaried ~$1,500-2,000/mo.

description: Rents the ransomware, breaks in, escalates, exfiltrates and deploys the payload against a victim they choose. Does the hands-on intrusion.
revenue_share_or_price: Affiliate keeps ~70-90% of the ransom (LockBit 80%; Qilin offers up to 85%)
evidence: DOJ: 'affiliate responsible for an attack would receive the remaining 80%'. NCA LockBit data: of 194 registered affiliates, up to 114 paid to join and never received a ransom (heavily skewed income)
source_title: LockBit leader unmasked and sanctioned
notes: 194 affiliates identified; 148 built attacks; 119 negotiated; 69 active after Op Cronos; 7,000+ attacks built Jun 2022-Feb 2024; 2,110+ victims drawn into negotiation.

description: Compromises networks/edge devices and sells the access to ransomware affiliates; the labour-division step that separates break-in from extortion.
revenue_share_or_price: Average access price fell from ~$1,427 (Q1 2023) to ~$439 (Q1 2026); example listings $400-$1,000
evidence: Chainalysis/Darkweb IQ: access price $1,427->$439; IAB on-chain income at least $14m in 2025 (~1/58 of ransom flows); IAB inflow spikes lead payments by ~30 days
source_title: Crypto ransomware 2026
notes: EclecticIQ (Global Group): IAB 'HuanEbashes' offered US law-firm RDP at $1,000 and a 'Brute VPN' tool at $400 (2025). Mandiant: access->hand-off time fell from >8h (2022) to 22s (2025).

description: Runs victim chat, applies pressure, sets leak deadlines, verifies payment. One of the slowest, least-automated steps.
revenue_share_or_price: No standard split; salaried or per-brand; the binding revenue constraint is victim willingness to pay (~20-28%)
evidence: LockBit panel leak: 4,442 negotiation messages over ~4 months across 75 accounts. Coveware: payment rate ~20-28% (record lows 2025-26)
source_title: Ransomware Marketplace Report Q4 2020
notes: Headcount for professional negotiators NOT FOUND. Prior project estimate: negotiation ~20% of affiliate labour hours.

description: Hosts stolen-data leak sites used for double extortion and for affiliate recruitment/marketing.
revenue_share_or_price: Part of operator overhead (bundled into the developer cut)
evidence: Maze pioneered public leaks (Allied Universal, Nov 2019); by Q4 2020, 70% of attacks threatened to leak data
source_title: Ransomware Marketplace Report Q4 2020
notes: Leak-site victim counts: ransomware.live 8,146 (2025), ~10,500 annualised 2026 (prior project).

description: Moves ransom crypto through mixers, OTC desks and exchanges to cash. Thin professional layer; an enforcement chokepoint.
revenue_share_or_price: Mixer-as-a-service commissions ~3-10%; 'Black U' sells illicit crypto 10-20% below market
evidence: FinCEN: 97% of reported ransomware payment transactions in Bitcoin, 2% Monero; collected in unhosted wallets then cashed out at exchanges. AudiA6 mixer (3-10%) received 10,333 BTC (~$389m) before June 2026 takedown
source_title: Ransomware Trends in Bank Secrecy Act Data 2022-2024
notes: AudiA6 figures via Chainalysis (prior project). Chinese-language laundering networks processed $16.1bn in 2025 (~20% of $82bn on-chain laundering).

description: Supplies resilient hosting, criminal VPN/proxy, loaders and crypters that defeat antivirus. Tool-and-infrastructure supply side.
revenue_share_or_price: Crypter add-ons ~$50/month (Blackhole era); disposable servers from ~$24/month (RedVDS)
evidence: Blackhole exploit kit: $500-700/month rental + $50/month crypter, 1,000+ customers (Paunch arrested Oct 2013). Op Endgame: one infrastructure supplier earned at least EUR 69m renting ransomware-deployment infrastructure
source_title: Meet Paunch, accused author of the Blackhole Exploit Kit
notes: EU sanctioned the Trickbot administrator 'Stern' (Jul 2026); associated wallets received $300m+ across 8 families.

description: Sells turnkey phishing/adversary-in-the-middle kits, domains and support; the demand side's shared toolchain.
revenue_share_or_price: Subscriptions from ~$88/week to ~$1,588/year (Lighthouse); 'thousands' of customers (Tycoon 2FA)
evidence: Tycoon 2FA ~62% of Microsoft-blocked phishing by mid-2025, 30m+ emails/month, 500,000+ orgs/month; Google RICO suit alleges Lighthouse hit 1m+ victims in 120+ countries
source_title: Crypto ransomware 2026 / prior project ransomware & phishing memos
notes: Tycoon/Lighthouse figures from Microsoft (2026-03-04) and Google (2025-11-12) via prior project phishing memo; not re-fetched this session (proxy 429).

description: Jailbroken or uncensored LLMs sold to criminals (WormGPT lineage, GhostGPT, Kriminal.ai, MessiahGPT). Mostly thin wrappers over mainstream models; many are scams.
revenue_share_or_price: WormGPT 4 $50/month, $175/year, $220 lifetime; MessiahGPT $9.99-$39.99/mo; Kriminal.ai $12.99/mo; original WormGPT EUR500-5,000
evidence: Unit 42 tested WormGPT 4 (571 Telegram subscribers) and KawaiiGPT: output usable but rudimentary, no confirmed incidents. Talos paid for FraudGPT and received non-working credentials (a scam)
source_title: The Dilemma of AI: Malicious LLMs
notes: MessiahGPT/Kriminal.ai prices from Flashpoint (2026-10-06). KELA: 'AI does not necessarily replace experienced malware developers'; buyers call uncensored models 'overrated'.

description: A low-skill actor uses an agentic coding tool to build and sell ransomware they could not otherwise write; lowers the skill floor rather than raising capability.
revenue_share_or_price: Ransomware variants/kits sold for $400-$1,200 on forums (Dread, CryptBB, Nulled)
evidence: Anthropic (GTG-5004, UK-based): actor appeared 'completely dependent on AI to develop functional malware' (ChaCha20+RSA, shadow-copy deletion, anti-debugging); banned
source_title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025
notes: GTG-5004 designation and UK attribution via BleepingComputer (2025-08-28); sold on Dread/CryptBB/Nulled. Single lab, self-reported.

description: A single operator uses an agentic coding tool to run recon, credential theft, intrusion and extortion against many victims; the AI makes tactical and strategic choices and sets ransom amounts from victims' finances.
revenue_share_or_price: Ransom demands sometimes exceeded $500,000
evidence: Anthropic (GTG-2002): at least 17 organisations across healthcare, emergency services, government and religious institutions in one operation; Claude chose what to exfiltrate and crafted demands
source_title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: August 2025
notes: Shows AI collapsing several pre-AI roles (intruder+negotiator+analyst) into one operator. Single lab, no independent victim confirmation.

description: An AI chatbot conducts ransom negotiations and applies psychological pressure, helping non-English-speaking affiliates and supporting seven-figure demands; humans review and set deadlines.
revenue_share_or_price: Offered inside an 85% affiliate revenue share; demands up to ~$1m (9.5 BTC)
evidence: EclecticIQ: Global Group RaaS (launched 2 Jun 2025, rebrand of BlackLock/Mamona) ran an AI-driven negotiation panel; 17 confirmed victims by 14 Jul 2025
source_title: GLOBAL GROUP: Emerging Ransomware-as-a-Service
notes: Exec summary says 80% affiliate share, body/Figure 10 say 85% (inconsistent). Corroborated by Picus via Axios (2025-07-29).

description: An AI agent executes the whole chain (recon -> credential theft -> lateral movement -> persistence -> encryption) with a human only provisioning infrastructure and choosing the victim.
revenue_share_or_price: No price model; ransom amount not stated (note used an example BTC address)
evidence: Sysdig JADEPUFFER: agent ran 600+ payloads end to end via Langflow RCE (CVE-2025-3248), encrypted 1,342 Nacos configs; 'skill floor for running ransomware has dropped to whatever it costs to run an agent'
source_title: JADEPUFFER: Agentic ransomware for automated database extortion
notes: Single vendor, behavioural inference, no model named, one victim environment. CSA: only two documented autonomous post-exploitation cases in 2026 ('not yet a statistically established trend').

description: Vendors sell face-swap/deepfake image and video generation for KYC bypass and impersonation, advertised openly on Telegram and guarantee marketplaces.
revenue_share_or_price: ~$10 per image to ~$500 per minute of video (2024)
evidence: Trend Micro: deepfake services advertised at $10/image to $500/min of video, used for KYC bypass. Xinbi and Huione guarantee markets list 'AI face swapping'/'AI deepfake tooling'
source_title: Back to the Hype: how cybercriminals are using GenAI
notes: Face-swap listing on Huione (Elliptic 2026-06-24); 'AI deepfake tooling' category on Xinbi (TRM 2026-02-06). No post-2024 price series or vendor/volume counts FOUND.

description: Huione-style Telegram guarantee marketplaces host AI/deepfake tool vendors alongside laundering, stolen data and KYC bypass, with escrow holding vendor deposits.
revenue_share_or_price: Not separately priced; cybercrime-service deposits 'run into the thousands of USDT'
evidence: Elliptic: Huione Guarantee received $31bn+ before going offline (Jun 2026), tracking 30+ active guarantee markets; a merchant panel advertised 'AI face swapping services'. Chainalysis: scams linked on-chain to AI vendors earn $3.2m/operation vs $719k (4.5x)
source_title: Behind the FBI case against Huione
notes: Chainalysis AI-vendor figures (crypto-scams-2026, 2026-01-13) are selection-biased to scammers who pay AI vendors on-chain. Deepfake vendor counts/volumes NOT FOUND.

description: AI agents and malware automate reconnaissance, credential harvesting and mass exploitation to obtain access at machine speed.
revenue_share_or_price: No distinct price; feeds the existing IAB and affiliate market
evidence: GTIG: PROMPTSTEAL (APT28, Jun 2025) first malware observed querying an LLM in live operations; GreyNoise PaperCut campaign (reported Sep 2026): hundreds of agents hit 395 organisations, 11 orgs in 26 seconds (objective unknown, no confirmed ransomware)
source_title: Threat Actor Usage of AI Tools
notes: PaperCut via GreyNoise/GRIT (prior project, 2026-09). GTIG: cost of premium model access/compute is 'one of the primary barriers'.

description: State-nexus actors run scheduled agent 'swarms' for standing collection; AI does 80-90% of tactical work, humans make 4-6 decisions per campaign.
revenue_share_or_price: N/A (state, not sold)
evidence: Anthropic GTG-1002 (assessed Chinese state): ~30 targets, AI performed 80-90% of tactical operations, 4-6 human decision points; thousands of requests, multiple per second; Claude hallucinated credentials (an obstacle to full autonomy)
source_title: Disrupting the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
notes: GTG-10007 (~50 orgs, 13 standing collection agents) and GTG-20006 (Russian, 20+ orgs) in Anthropic Sep 2026. Autonomy claims contested by outside researchers.

description: A market that has grown around the model-cost barrier: stolen API keys, pooled accounts, and reseller fraud selling 'discounted' frontier-model access.
revenue_share_or_price: Prices of stolen Gemini/Claude accounts more than doubled in 2026; '$5,000 lifetime' recon-platform licences seen
evidence: Anthropic GTG-50021 sold discounted 'Claude' access secretly routed to another model while harvesting buyers' credentials; GTG-50020 used stolen customer API keys against ~30 AI firms
source_title: Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026
notes: Anthropic Sep 2026 page NOT re-fetched this session (proxy 429); figures via prior project. Shows the cost barrier itself spawning criminal business models.

description: A crypto mixer exposes an agent interface (MCP server) so AI agents can order mixing automatically; forward-looking, no documented criminal use yet.
revenue_share_or_price: Mixer commissions apply; no distinct AI price
evidence: Elliptic: Flash Mixer is the first mixer publishing an MCP server, issuing single-use API keys to agents; 'an early signal of what agentic laundering will look like'; no documented criminal use
source_title: AI agents can now use a crypto mixer
notes: Forward-looking; included as the laundering-layer analogue of agentic attack tooling.

description: A subscription service pairing compromised-mailbox access with an AI assistant that reads inboxes, maps 'money movers', picks targets and drafts impersonation emails; largely 'vibe coded'.
revenue_share_or_price: $1,500 initiation + $500 recurring subscription (period not stated)
evidence: Microsoft DCU EvilTokens (launched Feb 2026): 12,000+ compromised inboxes across 10,000+ organisations; 'first action against an end-to-end AI-enabled cybercrime service'; 2 UK arrests (11 Sep 2026), 50 sites seized
source_title: Disrupting EvilTokens: the AI chatbot built for cybercrime
notes: Grade B: existence/scale corroborated by E.D. Va. civil action and UK arrests, though 'AI at every step' is Microsoft's characterisation. BEC segment, adjacent to ransomware.
